Interpolate a model into a solver-ready scenario

Source: R/interpolation.R
interpolate_model.Rd

Builds an interpolated scenario from a model via the mapping pipeline: collects sets from the model objects, builds the membership / calendar / lifespan / value / constraint / cost mappings, extracts and interpolates the numeric parameters over the milestone years, and (optionally) folds, prunes and validates the result. The returned scenario is ready for solve_model() / solve_scenario().

Usage

interpolate_model(
  object,
  name = NULL,
  ...,
  base = NULL,
  desc = NULL,
  ondisk = FALSE,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  fold = FALSE,
  sparse = TRUE,
  prune = TRUE,
  validate = TRUE,
  code = NULL,
  kvl = FALSE,
  boundary_prices = NULL,
  .prefilter = FALSE,
  parent_levels = getOption("energyRt.parent_levels", FALSE),
  fx_equ = getOption("energyRt.fx_equ", TRUE),
  on_missing_input = getOption("energyRt.on_missing_input", "stop"),
  verbose = isVerbose(),
  .reuse = NULL
)

# S4 method for class 'model'
interpolate(object, ...)

Arguments

object

as mod, for the method dispatched on a scenario.

name

character scenario name. If NULL, a default scen_<model> is used (with a warning).

...

additional energyRt objects folded into the model BEFORE the pipeline runs: settings, config, calendar, horizon, a whole repository, or individual model "bricks" (technology, commodity, storage, ...). This is how a scenario overrides or extends the model (e.g. pass a sampled calendar to interpolate on a reduced time resolution).

base

optional interpolated scenario to build on. The objects in ... must be new to the model: constraints, costs, taxes and subsidies, new processes and commodities, or a calendar / geoscale that samples the base's. The result is the base plus what they add: the base's tables are reused, nothing is written into its store, and the result equals a full interpolation of the model with the base's additions and the new ones. The base's fold, sparse and prune settings apply. Otherwise (another model, a replaced object, settings or horizon objects) a message says why and the model is interpolated in full. object may be the base itself.

New processes, commodities and other model objects are built on the base too: the per-object tables of the objects the base already holds are reused, the new objects' tables are computed, and every map is rebuilt.

desc

character scenario description.

ondisk

logical; store each parameter's data in the on-disk parameter store rather than the in-memory @data slot. FALSE (default) keeps data in memory, which the solver writers read directly; TRUE suits very large models (data is materialised back to memory at solve time).

overwrite

logical; overwrite an existing on-disk scenario of the same name.

fold

logical or character; whole-column "fold" of trimmable dimensions to NA wildcards to shrink the data. TRUE folds region + timeslice + year; FALSE (default) folds nothing; a character vector selects dims among region, timeslice, year, comm, tech, stg, trade. The wildcards are substituted by an artificial set member in the written model files only; the scenario object keeps them and getData() expands them.

A dimension folds only where the value is uniform across its WHOLE set, so folding never changes the solution — it changes how the same numbers are stored. year matters most in weather-heavy models: one weather series repeated across milestone years is usually the largest parameter, and region/timeslice alone do not touch it. Measured on a 4-region d365_h24 model over 7 milestones, adding year took pWeather from 245,259 to 35,037 rows (-85.7%) with a bit-identical objective on GLPK and Pyomo/HiGHS. A model whose weather genuinely differs by year simply does not fold.

sparse

logical; the storage knob, and the user-facing switch between drop_default_values() and expand_default_values(). TRUE drops value == defVal rows; FALSE materialises the default over each parameter's full domain (the form GAMS needs) and then trims rows no map indexes. Folding applies to either.

prune

logical; apply the per-parameter misc$prune$value filter via drop_default_values() - rows whose interpolated value equals that parameter's flagged value are dropped (lossless: an absent tuple reads as the default, which equals the dropped value). One parameter is flagged today (pWeather). Superseded by sparse's value = form; retained for compatibility.

validate

logical; run validate_scenario_parameters() after interpolation (schema, duplicate keys, map/parameter coverage, missing governing constraints, calendar chronology).

code

optional named list overriding solver source-code blocks (GLPK, GAMS, JuMP, PYOMOConcrete, ...), each either a script-file path or a character vector of lines. Lets a model-script version be supplied at interpolation time without rebuilding sysdata (handy to A/B templates).

kvl

logical or NULL; build the Kirchhoff voltage-law cycle constraints for meshed trade networks. NULL (default) engages them when the network has cycles and reactances to use.

boundary_prices

optional data.frame pricing import/export stubs for trade routes dropped by a SPATIAL SAMPLE (a geoscales::filter_geoscale() subset passed via ...); see subset_model_regions() for the columns. Ignored (with a warning) when no sampled geoscale is supplied.

.prefilter

EXPERIMENTAL, default FALSE. Restrict each model object's data to the timeslices and regions the SCENARIO declares before interpolating it, rather than interpolating everything and discarding the excess afterwards.

On the sampled-calendar recipe – a full-year model with a subset calendar handed to this function – the default order expands all 8,760 timeslices in ob2mi and then keeps 96. The parameter filters that follow are cheap (0.05s on a 5-node model); the cost is the interpolation they cannot undo.

Off by default because it is not obviously safe: anything deriving a relation from the full declared grid rather than from the calendar would see a narrower input. Compare objectives before relying on it.

parent_levels

logical or character; give a variable rows at every timeslice / region level COARSER than the one it occupies, each defined by a roll-up of its finer rows, so a constraint can be written at a level the variable does not natively carry (summand@timeframe / @geoframe). FALSE (default) builds none; TRUE builds them for every SUPPORTED variable; a character vector selects among those. Naming an unsupported variable is an error listing what is supported – a parent row with no equation to define it would be a free variable.

vOutTot / vInpTot carry their parent rows unconditionally and are not affected: eqOutTot / eqInpTot are written against them.

Defaults to getOption("energyRt.parent_levels", FALSE), so a whole run or test suite can be switched in one place.

fx_equ

logical; write a bound whose two sides coincide (.fx, or .lo == .up, with the same weather factors) as one equality row (eq<Family>Fx) instead of a pair of inequalities (eq<Family>Lo + eq<Family>Up). Applies to every bound family: technology availability (af, afs, afc), shares, capacity, new capacity and retirement of technologies, storages and trade, storage availability, charge, discharge, duration and part ratios, supply availability and reserve, trade flows and availability, import and export rows. The solution is the same; the model has fewer rows before presolve (-25% on an hourly full-year VRE model). FALSE writes the pairs. Defaults to getOption("energyRt.fx_equ", TRUE).

on_missing_input

"stop" or "warn": what to do when a process with existing capacity (stock, or a lower / fixed capacity bound) is declared in a region where one of its input commodities has no source. "stop" names the cells; "warn" drops them, as is always done for processes that could only be built new. Defaults to getOption("energyRt.on_missing_input", "stop").

verbose

logical; print per-step progress. This also governs the variant-expansion report – how many process objects were expanded and how many constraints were generated for them. The generated constraints themselves are retrievable with getObject(scen, class = "constraint"); each carries a readable desc and, in misc$.variant_source, the object it was derived from.

.reuse

internal: an interpolated scenario whose per-object tables are reused for the objects it holds (set by base).

Value

an interpolated scenario object.

See also

solve_model(), solve_scenario(), the interpolate S4 method.

Other interpolation: subset_model_regions(), with_solver_log()

Examples

# \donttest{
ek  <- topia$modules$electricity$R3
mod <- newModel("TOPIA", data = ek$repo,
                calendar = topia$modules$calendars$s4_h24,
                region = ek$regions,
                horizon = topia$modules$horizons$base,
                discount = 0.05)
mod <- setGeoscale(mod, ek$geoscale)

# build the solver-facing sets and parameters; nothing is solved yet
scen <- interpolate_model(mod, name = "BASE")
#> Cost declared at a coarse geoscale level:
#>   TBD_COA_WEST_CENTRAL@invcost: CENTRAL, WEST
#>   TBD_GAS_WEST_CENTRAL@invcost: CENTRAL, WEST
#> The cost is charged ONCE at that cell rather than at each child region, and is discounted at the children's rate. That is usually what a national cost datum means -- said here because it is a different number from naming the children individually.
scen
#> Name:  BASE 
#> Model:
#> Name:  TOPIA 

# `fold = TRUE` substitutes constant parameters into the equations, which
# shrinks what the backend has to read
model_size(interpolate_model(mod, name = "FOLDED", fold = TRUE))
#> Cost declared at a coarse geoscale level:
#>   TBD_COA_WEST_CENTRAL@invcost: CENTRAL, WEST
#>   TBD_GAS_WEST_CENTRAL@invcost: CENTRAL, WEST
#> The cost is charged ONCE at that cell rather than at each child region, and is discounted at the children's rate. That is usually what a national cost datum means -- said here because it is a different number from naming the children individually.
#> model_size: FOLDED
#>   parameters : 200 value, 359 maps, 15 sets
#>   param rows : 2,111  (fold step: 8,741 -> 2,111, saved 6,630 = 76%)
#>   folded dims: region=20  timeslice=11  year=19
#>   estimate   : ~61,849 variables, ~63,464 constraints (from gating maps)
#>   top parameters by rows:
#>     pWeather           753
#>     pDemand            384
#>     pTimesliceAgg      297
#>     pExportRow         288
#>     pTimesliceShare    101
#>     pTechStock         50
#>     pTechFixom         28
#>     pTechInvcost       28
#>     pTechEac           20
#>     pTechCinp2use      16
#>     pDiscountFactor    15
#>     pTechStockSurv     12
#>     pTradeIrVarom      8
#>     pTradeIrEff        8
#>     pSupCost           7
# }
